archetype.name: Bubble Team (out-chanced, finishing-reliant)
archetype.definition: A team hovering near .500 after a playoff season, kept afloat by a productive top unit and above-average shooting while its 5-on-5 play rates among the league's worst.

report.headline: Out-chanced and leaning on finishing; last spring's playoff gains look in danger.
report.take:
Anaheim arrives at the end of October 5-6-0, fifth in the Pacific and 25th of 32 on the site. That is a sharp step back from a 2025-26 season that produced 92 standings points, a 16th-place site rank and six playoff wins. The record is not the worst part. At 5-on-5 the Ducks hold an xGF % of 0.44, 27th in the league, and they put just 23.5 shots on goal a game, 29th and well under the league's 27.4. Last season's xGF % was 0.519. This one looks much more like 2024-25's 0.451, the year that ended 28th on the site.

What keeps the offense respectable, 19th in goals a game, is finishing and a handful of forwards. The skaters shoot 12.4% in all situations, ninth in the league and above the 11.3% average. Leo Carlsson has 13 points, eight of them on a power play converting 22.2%, and Beckett Sennecke has six goals on 28 shots while leading the forwards at 20.69 minutes a night. A team that shoots this little needs that kind of conversion to score at all, and conversion is the least reliable thing in hockey.

The goaltending numbers need reading together. A .882 team save % ranks 25th, but the goalies are +2.7 in GSAx, 13th, and graded B-. Lukas Dostal and Ville Husso are stopping slightly more than the chances warrant, so the poor save % reflects the quality of what gets through. The 5-on-5 PDO of 100.2 and the all-situation 100.6, exactly league average, say the overall luck is neutral, and a Pts vs Goal Diff of -0.7 says the close games haven't hurt much either. A 5-6 record with a -5 goal differential is about what this team has earned. The risk is in the mix: shooting that will cool and defending that won't fix itself.

The last five games show where the floor is: 1-4, 12 scored and 20 allowed, inside a five-game losing streak that only ended with a 5-4 win in Philadelphia. The season pace of 75 points is below even the 80 of 2024-25. Unless the shot share recovers toward last year's level, Anaheim is a team fighting for the edges of the playoff race rather than inside it.

strengths.title: Carlsson and a productive power play
strengths.body: Carlsson leads the team with 13 points, eight on the power play, and the unit's 22.2% ranks 12th, above the league's 21.2%. It is a real step up from 11.8% two seasons ago and 18.6% last year, so it doesn't look like a fluke. For a team that struggles to create at even strength, the power play is the most dependable source of goals it has.

strengths.title: Goalies better than their save %
strengths.body: The team save % of .882 ranks 25th, but the goalies are +2.7 in GSAx, 13th, with Dostal at +1.6 over eight starts. They are stopping more than an average goalie would on these shots. The low save % comes from dangerous chances against, not poor goaltending. That gives the Ducks a stable piece to build on, but it won't save the team on its own.

strengths.title: Luneau driving play on the blue line
strengths.body: Tristan Luneau has a 0.555 xGF % in nearly 21 minutes a night, the best mark among the regulars and well above the team's 0.44. On a blueline graded D+, he is the one defenseman consistently tilting the ice. It is a small sample, but it is the clearest sign of a pairing that can be trusted.

concerns.title: Losing the 5-on-5 battle badly
concerns.body: An xGF % of 0.44 (27th) and 23.5 shots a game (29th) mean Anaheim is chasing play most nights. Granlund (0.377) and Gauthier (0.38) are being out-chanced heavily in big minutes. This is a reversal from last season's 0.519, and it was also the profile in 2024-25, so it may be the team's baseline rather than a slump.

concerns.title: Scoring propped up by shooting %
concerns.body: Skaters shoot 12.4%, ninth in the league and above the 11.3% average, on very low volume. When that conversion drifts back, a team this shot-starved loses goals quickly. Gauthier, with only two goals on a team-high 34 shots, should rise and offset some of it, but that won't cover the team-wide drop.

concerns.title: Top pair caved in, wingers feasting
concerns.body: Jackson LaCombe plays 26.18 minutes a night with a 0.358 xGF %, and Noah Warren's 0.356 is no better. Opposing wingers are scoring well above their norms against this defense, which ranks 30th by that measure. With the PK at 76.2% (21st), the result is 3.36 goals allowed a game, and it was four a game over the last five.

trend.note: A 4-1 stretch early in October gave way to a five-game losing streak. The last five went 1-4 with a .200 points %, and the defense allowed four goals a game, worse than its season rate.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games, two against the league's worst goaltending
weekAhead.body:
This is the softest week Anaheim could ask for: three games at home, the first two against teams ranked 32nd and 26th on the site. Vancouver is last at nearly everything that matters. It allows 33.5 shots a game, has goalies at -6.4 GSAx and kills only 64.4% of penalties, so even a low-volume attack should get real looks. Buffalo is a tougher test than its rank suggests, controlling play with a 0.53 CF % and 0.511 xGF %, both better than Anaheim's. But its goalies have the league's worst save % at .866, and its 10.5% power play won't punish the Ducks' shaky PK.

Ottawa closes the week as the real test. The Senators are 8-4-0, allow only 23.3 shots a game (fifth) and rank eighth in goals against. A 5-on-5 PDO of 103 suggests some of that is running hot. Their power play is just 11.5%, which again protects Anaheim's weak penalty kill. Anything less than two wins in three home games would be a bad sign.

keyMatchups.title: Ducks' power play vs Vancouver's kill
keyMatchups.body: Anaheim's 22.2% power play meets the league's worst penalty kill at 64.4%. Carlsson, with eight PP points, is the man to watch. This is the clearest edge of the week.

keyMatchups.title: Anaheim wingers vs soft defenses
keyMatchups.body: Vancouver (32nd) and Buffalo (31st) give up the most to wingers of any teams in the league. That is a chance for Sennecke to keep scoring and for Gauthier to finally turn his shot volume into goals.

keyMatchups.title: Generating shots against Ottawa
keyMatchups.body: Ottawa allows just 23.3 shots a game and Anaheim produces 23.5, so this game sets a stingy defense against a quiet attack. Anaheim's high shooting % will have to hold up here, and Dostal's GSAx edge matters most in a game this tight.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Anaheim can push its shot totals well above its 23.5 a game against Vancouver and Buffalo. If it can't do that against these two, the low shot share is a structural problem rather than the schedule.

restOfSeason.body:
Of what Anaheim has done, the goaltending and the power play look most sustainable. The goalies are slightly above expected and the PP has improved over two seasons. The shooting % is the piece most likely to regress, and with this little shot volume that would pull scoring below its current 2.91 a game. Nothing in the luck measures points to a big bounce coming: overall PDO is league average and close games have been close to neutral. Improvement has to come from the 5-on-5 game, and last season's 0.519 xGF % shows this core has played better. I expect the shot share to recover only partway, to roughly 0.45-0.49, which points to a final total of about 74-86 standings points.

That range sits mostly below last year's 92. It leaves Anaheim chasing a wild-card spot rather than holding one, with an upper end that depends on the blueline in front of LaCombe getting out-chanced less and on the young forwards adding shot volume.
swingFactors: 5-on-5 shot share recovering toward last year's level
LaCombe's pairing stabilizing in heavy minutes

confidence.note: Only 11 games, and a big swing from last season's play makes the baseline uncertain.
